Q. The length of an iron rod is measured by a brass scale. When both of them are at 10°C,
the measured length is 50.0 cm. What is the length of the rod at 40°C when measured by
the brass scale at 40°C? (  for brass = 24×10–6 °C–1,  for iron = 16×10–6°C–1)
Length of brass scale at 10°C( l10b ) =Length of iron rod at 10°C ( l10I ) = 50.0 cm
Length of iron rod at 40°C ( l40I ) =?
Length of 1 cm division of the brass scale at 40°C
Therefore, the length of the rod as measured by the brass scale at 40°C = 50.024 1.00072
Hence, the length of the rod at 40°C is 49.99 cm.
Expansion in brass scale = 𝑙 𝛼𝑏 ∆𝜃 Expansion in iron rod = 𝑙 𝛼𝑠 ∆𝜃 The difference in expansion between brass scale and iron rod = 𝑙(𝛼𝑏 − 𝛼𝑠)∆𝜃 = 50.0(24 x10-6 – 16x10-6)30
Since the expansion of the scale is more than that of the rod, the scale will read less reading by 0.012cm. Therefore, the observed length of the rod will be (50.0-0.012) = 49.988cm = 49.99 cm.
Q. A second's pendulum made of brass keeps the correct time at 10°C. How many seconds will it lose or gain per day when the temperature of its surroundings rises to 35°C? (αb = 2× 10–5 K–1)
Loss or gain of time per day =?
1 Loss in time = 2 αbT ×duration of time 1 = 2 αb (35 -10) × 1 day = 0.5 × 2x10-5× 25 × 86400 = 21.6 = 22 s Hence loss in time per day is 22 s
